# Task Management System for thos

## Context

The thos dashboard currently orchestrates Claude agents but has no way to organize work at a higher level. This adds a hybrid task management system where users create tasks (title, description, status, priority) and can optionally delegate any task to a Claude agent. Agent completion auto-updates the linked task's status.

## Architecture

Follows existing patterns exactly: WebSocket messages for communication, file-based JSON for persistence, React state in the `useWebSocket` hook.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Types — `lib/types.ts`

Add after the UI state section:

**Task model:**
```typescript
type TaskStatus = "todo" | "in-progress" | "done"
type TaskPriority = "low" | "medium" | "high" | "urgent"

interface Task {
  id: string
  title: string
  description: string
  status: TaskStatus
  priority: TaskPriority
  agentId: string | null    // linked agent when delegated
  createdAt: number
  updatedAt: number
}
```

**Browser → Server messages** (add to `BrowserMessage` union):
- `BrowserCreateTask` — `{ type: "create_task", title, description, priority }`
- `BrowserUpdateTask` — `{ type: "update_task", taskId, updates: Partial<Pick<Task, title|description|status|priority>> }`
- `BrowserDeleteTask` — `{ type: "delete_task", taskId }`
- `BrowserDelegateTask` — `{ type: "delegate_task", taskId }`

**Server → Browser messages** (add to `ServerMessage` union):
- `ServerTaskList` — `{ type: "task_list", tasks: Task[] }`
- `ServerTaskUpdated` — `{ type: "task_updated", task: Task }`
- `ServerTaskDeleted` — `{ type: "task_deleted", taskId }`

### 2. Persistence — new `server/task-store.ts`

Single-file storage at `$TMPDIR/thos-tasks/tasks.json` (tasks are small, no need for per-file storage). Mirrors `SessionStore` pattern with debounced and sync write methods. Methods: `loadAll()`, `save()`, `saveSync()`, `flush()`.

### 3. Server — modify `server/ws.ts`

- Import `TaskStore`, instantiate alongside `SessionStore`
- Add `tasks` Map + `restoreTasks()` on startup
- Add `broadcastTaskList()` and `persistTasks()` helpers
- Handle 4 new browser message types in `handleBrowserMessage` switch:
  - `create_task` — create task, persist, broadcast
  - `update_task` — update fields, persist, broadcast
  - `delete_task` — remove from map, persist, broadcast
  - `delegate_task` — call existing `spawnClaude(prompt)` with task description, link `agentId`, set status to `in-progress`
- Auto-update linked task when agent finishes: in the CLI disconnect handler (`ws.on("close")`), if agent status becomes `"done"`, find linked task and mark it `"done"`
- Send task list in `sendFullStateToSocket()` on browser connect
- Flush tasks in `shutdown()`

### 4. Client hook — modify `hooks/use-websocket.ts`

- Add `tasks` state: `useState<Task[]>([])`
- Handle `task_list`, `task_updated`, `task_deleted` server messages
- Add action callbacks: `createTask`, `updateTask`, `deleteTask`, `delegateTask`
- Return all new state and actions

### 5. UI Components — 3 new files

**`components/dashboard/task-panel.tsx`** — Main container
- Header with "Tasks" title and "+" button to toggle create form
- Scrollable list of tasks grouped by status: In Progress → Todo → Done (collapsed)
- Each group has a label header
- Receives all task actions as props

**`components/dashboard/task-card.tsx`** — Individual task card
- Compact card showing: priority badge (color-coded), title, truncated description
- Status badge: `todo` = outline, `in-progress` = blue, `done` = green with strikethrough title
- Priority colors: `urgent` = red, `high` = orange, `medium` = yellow, `low` = muted
- Action buttons: cycle status on click, delegate (Play icon), delete (Trash2 icon)
- When linked to an agent (`agentId` set), show "View Agent" link
- Inline edit mode for title/description (similar to existing rename pattern in agent-sidebar)

**`components/dashboard/task-create-form.tsx`** — Inline creation form
- Title input, description textarea, priority select (default: medium)
- "Create" button, compact form matching existing input styles

### 6. Dashboard layout — modify `app/dashboard/page.tsx`

- Destructure new task values from `useWebSocket()`
- Add `showTasks` toggle state
- Render `TaskPanel` as a conditional right column (`w-80 border-l`)
- Layout: `AgentSidebar (w-56)` | `Chat (flex-1)` | `TaskPanel (w-80, toggleable)`
- Pass `onSelectAgent` to TaskPanel so clicking a linked agent navigates to it

### 7. Toggle button — modify `components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx`

- Add `ListTodo` icon button to the status bar for toggling the task panel
- Accept `onToggleTasks` and `showTasks` props

## File Change Summary

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `lib/types.ts` | Modify — add Task types + message types + update unions |
| `server/task-store.ts` | **Create** — file-based task persistence |
| `server/ws.ts` | Modify — task CRUD handlers, auto-status, broadcast |
| `hooks/use-websocket.ts` | Modify — task state, message handlers, action callbacks |
| `components/dashboard/task-panel.tsx` | **Create** — task list container |
| `components/dashboard/task-card.tsx` | **Create** — individual task card |
| `components/dashboard/task-create-form.tsx` | **Create** — task creation form |
| `components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx` | Modify — add toggle button |
| `app/dashboard/page.tsx` | Modify — wire task panel into layout |

## Implementation Order

1. `lib/types.ts` (no dependencies)
2. `server/task-store.ts` (depends on types)
3. `server/ws.ts` (depends on types + task-store)
4. `hooks/use-websocket.ts` (depends on types)
5. `components/dashboard/task-card.tsx` (depends on types)
6. `components/dashboard/task-create-form.tsx` (depends on types)
7. `components/dashboard/task-panel.tsx` (depends on card + form)
8. `components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx` (minor change)
9. `app/dashboard/page.tsx` (wire everything together)

## Verification

1. Start dev server (`pnpm dev`) — both Next.js and WS server should start
2. Open dashboard, verify task toggle button appears in status bar
3. Click toggle — task panel slides in on the right
4. Create a task (title + description + priority) — should appear in "Todo" group
5. Click status badge to cycle status → verify persistence (refresh page, task should persist)
6. Click delegate → verify a new agent spawns with the task description as prompt
7. When the agent completes → verify the linked task auto-updates to "done"
8. Delete a task → verify it disappears and is removed from disk

2. **File-based JSON storage**: Match the existing SessionStore pattern for persistence.
3. **Integrated in dashboard**: Embedded within the current dashboard layout.

- `app/dashboard/page.tsx` - Dashboard page, orchestrates layout
- `components/dashboard/agent-sidebar.tsx` - Agent list sidebar
- `components/dashboard/chat.tsx` - Chat component

- `server/session-store.ts` - File-based JSON persistence
- `lib/types.ts` - Shared type definitions
- `components/ui/button.tsx` - Button component (CVA variants)
- `components/ui/card.tsx` - Card component

- Stores JSON files in `$TMPDIR/thos-sessions/<id>.json`

- New types to add to lib/types.ts
- New TaskStore class (server/task-store.ts)
- New WebSocket message types for task CRUD
- New React components for the task UI
- Modifications to existing files (dashboard page, useWebSocket hook, ws.ts server)
- The plan should be specific about what goes where but not overly verbose

The task management system is fully implemented. Here's a summary of what was built:

## What was added

**New files (4):**
- `server/task-store.ts` — File-based JSON persistence for tasks (mirrors SessionStore pattern)
- `components/dashboard/task-card.tsx` — Individual task card with priority/status badges, inline editing, delegate/delete actions
- `components/dashboard/task-create-form.tsx` — Compact inline form for creating tasks
- `components/dashboard/task-panel.tsx` — Panel container with tasks grouped by status (In Progress → Todo → Done)

**Modified files (5):**
- `lib/types.ts` — Added `Task`, `TaskStatus`, `TaskPriority` types + 4 browser message types + 3 server message types
- `server/ws.ts` — Task CRUD handlers, auto-status update when agent finishes, task list broadcast on connect, shutdown flush
- `hooks/use-websocket.ts` — Task state, server message handlers, action callbacks (`createTask`, `updateTask`, `deleteTask`, `delegateTask`)
- `components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx` — Added ListTodo toggle button
- `components/dashboard/chat.tsx` — Passes task toggle props through to StatusBar
- `app/dashboard/page.tsx` — Wires task panel as toggleable right column (w-80)

## How to use

1. Run `pnpm dev` to start both Next.js and the WS server
2. Open `/dashboard` — click the list icon in the status bar to toggle the task panel
3. Click `+` to create a task (title, description, priority)
4. Click status badges to cycle: todo → in-progress → done
5. Click the play icon to **delegate** a task to a Claude agent — it spawns an agent with the task as prompt
6. When a delegated agent finishes, the linked task auto-completes
7. Tasks persist to disk (`$TMPDIR/thos-tasks/tasks.json`) and survive server restarts

The list icon is in the **status bar** at the top of the chat panel — it's the small `ListTodo` icon button on the far right, after the "agent: status" text.

Look for it here in the top bar:

```
thos dashboard          ws connected | agent: idle | [📋]
```

It's rendered by `components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx:52-60`. It appears after a `|` separator, right at the end of the status indicators. When the task panel is open, the icon highlights in the primary (golden) color.

If you're having trouble seeing it, it might be because the icon is quite small (`size-3.5`) and uses the `ghost` variant which has no background. Would you like me to make it more prominent — for example, adding a text label next to it or increasing the size?

1→# thos
     2→
     3→**the orchestrator you never knew you needed**
     4→
     5→A visual orchestration layer for [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code). Not another IDE — a UI that sits on top of the terminal-based agents you already use, solving the real friction of working with them day-to-day.
     6→
     7→## The Problem
     8→
     9→AI coding agents are powerful, but the experience of *using* them has real gaps:
    10→
    11→- **You lose track of what's happening.** Multiple agents running across tasks, and you're tab-switching and scrolling terminals to figure out who's doing what. The visibility problem compounds fast.
    12→
    13→- **Agents are smart but have the memory of an infant.** Your workflows are specific to you — your project structure, your preferences, your domain knowledge. The agent doesn't retain any of it between sessions. You end up re-explaining the same context over and over. A static CLAUDE.md helps, but it doesn't learn from your conversations or evolve with your codebase.
    14→
    15→- **Your machine is the bottleneck.** You have a laptop, not a build server. Agents want to compile, test, run — and your local machine can't keep up.
    16→
    17→- **Undoing things is painful.** Agent makes a wrong turn, and now you're doing forensics. Better change tracking, rollback, and context management should be table stakes — not an afterthought.
    18→
    19→- **Task management is manual.** Coordinating what gets done, in what order, across which agents — that's on you, in your head, with no tooling to help.
    20→
    21→## What thos Is
    22→
    23→thos is a UI wrapper around Claude Code. Terminals are fine — but when you're orchestrating work across agents, you need something more visual.
    24→
    25→Think of it as a control plane:
    26→
    27→- **Agent dashboard** — see what every agent is doing, in real time, at a glance
    28→- **Persistent memory** — agents that learn from your conversations and retain domain knowledge across sessions. Not just saved prompts — context that evolves with your codebase and workflows, so the first time you explain something is the last time.
    29→- **Change management** — track, diff, and roll back agent-generated changes with confidence
    30→- **Task orchestration** — assign, sequence, and track work across agents
    31→- **Remote access** — web UI accessible via localhost, with the option to expose over your network as needed
    32→
    33→## What thos Is Not
    34→
    35→- **Not an IDE.** VS Code, Cursor, Zed — these are well-engineered. thos doesn't compete with them; it complements them.
    36→- **Not a terminal replacement.** The terminal is the execution layer. thos is the visibility and coordination layer on top.
    37→- **Not a general agent framework.** Focused on Claude Code first. Breadth comes later, if it makes sense.
    38→
    39→## Prior Art
    40→
    41→Similar space as [superset.sh](https://superset.sh) and [Conductor](https://conductor.sh) — tools that recognize the gap between raw agent capability and the UX of actually orchestrating agent work.
    42→
    43→## Architecture
    44→
    45→### WebSocket relay server (`server/ws.ts`)
    46→
    47→A standalone WebSocket server on port 9900, started alongside Next.js via `concurrently`. Two connection families:
    48→
    49→- **`/browser`** — React dashboard connects here. Supports multiple tabs simultaneously.
    50→- **`/claude/:agentId`** — each Claude CLI connects here (passed as `--sdk-url`).
    51→
    52→The server acts as a relay: browser spawns agents, the server launches `claude` inside tmux sessions, and all CLI NDJSON messages are forwarded to the browser as `{ type: "relay", agentId, message }`.
    53→
    54→### Session persistence (`server/session-store.ts`)
    55→
    56→Agent state and full message history are persisted to `$TMPDIR/thos-sessions/<agentId>.json`. This means:
    57→
    58→- **Page refresh** restores all conversations — the server replays `message_history` to each connecting browser.
    59→- **Server restart** restores agents from disk. On startup, the server checks which tmux sessions are still alive (`tmux list-sessions`) and marks agents accordingly — `disconnected` if the tmux session survived, `done` if it didn't.
    60→- **Multiple browser tabs** see the same state — `sendToBrowser` iterates a `Set<WebSocket>` of all connected browsers.
    61→
    62→Writes are **debounced** (150ms) for high-frequency streaming events and **synchronous** for critical state changes (spawn, result, status transitions). On `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`, all agents are flushed to disk. **Tmux sessions are intentionally preserved** — they survive server restarts and shutdowns, so a quick server bounce doesn't destroy running CLI processes.
    63→
    64→### CLI resilience
    65→
    66→| Scenario | Behavior |
    67→|----------|----------|
    68→| CLI process exits or crashes | Status becomes `"done"`, agent moves to the Archived section in the sidebar. Browser sees "CLI session ended". |
    69→| Server restarts | Agents restored from disk. Tmux sessions are preserved — if a session is still alive, the agent is marked `"disconnected"`; otherwise `"done"`. |
    70→| Message sent while CLI is down | Queued in `pendingMessages[]`, flushed if/when the CLI WebSocket reconnects |
    71→| CLI reconnects (manual) | Browser sees "CLI reconnected", queued messages are delivered |
    72→
    73→> **Note:** Claude CLI's `--resume` flag does not reliably reconnect to a previous `--sdk-url` conversation, so automatic relaunch was removed. Ended agents are archived as read-only.
    74→
    75→### Agent status lifecycle
    76→
    77→```
    78→idle → spawning → connected ⇄ thinking → done
    79→                                           ↑
    80→                 disconnected ─────────────┘ (CLI exit/crash)
    81→                      │
    82→                    error
    83→```
    84→
    85→- `idle` — no process, ready to spawn
    86→- `spawning` — tmux session created, waiting for CLI WebSocket
    87→- `connected` — CLI connected, `system/init` received
    88→- `thinking` — waiting for assistant response
    89→- `done` — CLI finished or disconnected (terminal state)
    90→- `disconnected` — restored from disk with a live tmux session but no CLI WebSocket
    91→- `error` — unrecoverable failure
    92→
    93→Agents with status `done`, `disconnected`, or `error` are **archived** — they appear in a separate sidebar section and their chat is read-only ("This session has ended").
    94→
    95→### Message flow
    96→
    97→```
    98→Browser                    WS Server                    Claude CLI
    99→  │                           │                            │
   100→  │──spawn(prompt)──────────▶│                            │
   101→  │                           │──tmux new-session──────▶│
   102→  │◀──spawned(agentId)───────│                            │
   103→  │                           │◀──hook_response───────────│
   104→  │                           │──user(prompt)────────────▶│
   105→  │◀──relay(system/init)─────│◀──system/init──────────────│
   106→  │◀──relay(assistant)───────│◀──assistant─────────────────│
   107→  │◀──relay(control_request)─│◀──control_request──────────│
   108→  │──control_response───────▶│──control_response─────────▶│
   109→  │◀──relay(result)──────────│◀──result────────────────────│
   110→  │                           │                            │
   111→  │  (page refresh)           │                            │
   112→  │──connect /browser────────▶│                            │
   113→  │◀──agent_list─────────────│                            │
   114→  │◀──message_history────────│  (replays all stored msgs) │
   115→```
   116→
   117→### Agent management
   118→
   119→Right-click (or click the kebab icon) on any agent in the sidebar to open a context menu:
   120→
   121→| Action | When available | What it does |
   122→|--------|---------------|--------------|
   123→| **Rename** | Always | Swaps the label for an inline input (Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel) |
   124→| **Kill** | `spawning`, `connected`, `thinking` | Kills the tmux session + CLI WebSocket, sets status to `"done"` — agent moves to Archived |
   125→| **Clear History** | Always | Wipes the agent's message history on server and all connected browsers |
   126→| **Delete** | Always | Confirmation prompt, then permanently removes the agent from the Map, disk, and sidebar |

- `BrowserControlResponse` — Allow/deny tool approval

- `BrowserDeleteAgent` — Permanently delete an agent
- `BrowserRenameAgent` — Update agent label
- `BrowserClearHistory` — Wipe message history

- `ServerRelay` — Relay raw Claude NDJSON message to browser
- `ServerStatus` — Agent status change notification
- `ServerError` — Error report

- `ServerMessageHistory` — Full message history on connect

- `ServerHistoryCleared` — History cleared confirmation

- `ToolCallInfo` — Tool name + toolUseId

  - `save()` — Debounced write (150ms) for streaming messages
  - `saveSync()` — Synchronous write for critical state changes
  - `load()` / `loadAll()` — Load persisted agents on startup
  - `remove()` — Delete an agent's persisted file
  - `flushAll()` — Synchronous flush on shutdown

type TaskStatus = "todo" | "in-progress" | "done"

  id: string
  title: string
  description: string
  status: TaskStatus
  priority: TaskPriority
  agentId: string | null    // linked agent when delegated
  createdAt: number
  updatedAt: number
}

- `BrowserDeleteTask` — `{ type: "delete_task", taskId }`
- `BrowserDelegateTask` — `{ type: "delegate_task", taskId }`

- `ServerTaskList` — `{ type: "task_list", tasks: Task[] }`
